caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the prosystem_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

The armhf artifact has no libstdc++ dependency, so it clears every captured provider ceiling; ARM64 is bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced both ABI artifacts, resolver metadata, and package byte for byte. The selected github-actions/simulated/local-docker and reproduction local/native/local-docker identities remain explicit; evidence record hashes differ because runner profile, timestamps, run paths, run IDs, and build-log hashes are evidence-bearing fields.

The pristine source is commit 363b6dfbd3e240762e022c2b4897b4fe55722be3, tree 197be1b53019d95ed06658c2a801d0812ef76cf2, with no submodules. Commit-derived GIT_VERSION '-363b6df' is bound to all 32 C compiles per ABI and the exact 32-object C link; both binaries embed '1.3e-363b6df', while resolver metadata reports display version 1.3e.

Each ABI emits exactly one reviewed upstream unused-value warning at core/ProSystem.c:272. Parallel make output places that same four-line warning block differently between runs, so raw log hashes differ, but both order-insensitive fail-closed proofs bind the complete compile and link commands and reject any missing, changed, or extra warning, error, fatal error, or undefined reference.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and GLIBC_2.29 and records the AArch64 loader, libc, and libm. ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, reaches GLIBC_2.7, and records only libc and libm. Neither shared object has a PT_INTERP; loader, rootfs, frontend, and target execution remain runtime gates.
Resolver metadata declares GPLv2; any public distribution or release remains a human legal/policy and corresponding-source gate even though local builds reproduce.

Atari 7800 a78/bin/cdf loading, controllers, audio/video pacing, saves, deterministic states, cartridge compatibility, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates. Resolver metadata marks 7800 BIOS (U).rom optional and no BIOS is packaged, so BIOS discovery and compatibility require separately supplied lawful firmware during runtime validation.

The software-only Unix recipe produces one shared artifact per ABI/build profile and provides no basis for device-specific duplicate builds. ARM64 is build-identity-bound only to ra64-universal-v1, while ARMHF is bound only to ra32-a30-v1. Its modest ARMHF GLIBC floor makes ra32-mini-v0 and ra32-universal-v0 plausible candidates, but provider, build-identity, frontend, and runtime capture are absent; all device views remain ineligible.
